identity: The Muallaqa of Antara ibn Shaddad: a pre-Islamic Arabic qasida (ode) in the kamil metre, rhyming throughout in -m (mimiyya), 89 abyat, transmitted in diwan layout. Register is archaic, highly figurative classical verse; the movement is the standard qasida arc -- nasib at the ruined campsite and longing for Abla, then the rihla describing the she-camel, then fakhr (self-praise in battle) closing on the sons of Damdam. Each paragraph line here is exactly one bayt, carrying its two hemistichs (sadr and ajuz) run together on the same line. Source is an unpunctuated diwan rendering: token 33 is written joined as YADAR rather than YA DAR, and bayt 32 carries the definite article split off from its noun.
law: The sentence unit is the BAYT, one per paragraph line -- nothing smaller. Three convergent grounds. (1) Genre: in a qasida the bayt is by definition the complete, self-standing utterance, and the sadr/ajuz division inside it is METRICAL, not syntactic. (2) Internal proof: at indices 326-327 the text reads AL | WAHSHI, i.e. the definite article is severed from its own noun exactly at the hemistich seam of bayt 32. A seam that can cut a single WORD in half is not a place where a sentence can end -- anywhere in this document. (3) The format declares the paragraph-final mark ALWAYS correct even where syntax plainly runs on past it (bayt 17 ends at 177 and bayt 18 opens with AW coordinating back to its KA-ANNA; bayt 25 ends at 258 and bayt 26 continues with adjectives on SHADANIYYA; bayts 73-75 form one LAMMA...AYQANTU period across three forced marks; bayt 86 ends at 896 and bayt 87 opens with AL-SHATIMI, an adjective on IBNAY DAMDAM). Since the mark is imposed by layout against syntax, the governing unit is the printed verse line, not the clause. Therefore: boundaries fall at the last token of every bayt and nowhere else -- 89 in total, zero internal.
reasoning: I walked all 89 abyat and found exactly four sites where a mid-line break is arguable. Every one of them falls precisely on the hemistich seam, which is the single fact that disposes of all four. SITE i=4 (MUTARADDAM), bayt 0: HAL GHADARA... | AM HAL ARAFTA... Two interrogatives, and AM before HAL is readable as munqatia (bal + hamza), which would start a fresh question. Rejected: AM is still the correlative of the opening HAL, making one disjunctive question, and the seam is metrical. SITE i=572 (THIYABAHU), bayt 56: FA-SHAKAKTU BI-L-RUMHI... | LAYSA AL-KARIMU ALA AL-QANA BI-MUHARRAMI. The ajuz is a free-standing gnomic maxim with its own subject and predicate -- the strongest structural case in the poem. Rejected: it is the aphoristic gloss on the act just narrated, bound to it as commentary; editions set it off with a comma or dash, not a stop. SITE i=653 (LAHU), bayt 64: YA SHATA QANASIN LI-MAN HALLAT LAHU | HARUMAT ALAYYA WA-LAYTAHA LAM TAHRUMI. Vocative plus rhetorical question, then a declarative lament -- the site most likely to carry a question mark in a modern edition. Rejected: this source carries no punctuation at all (no non-Arabic token survives except NL), so no interrogative stop existed to be removed; and the seam is metrical. SITE i=695 (NIMATI), bayt 68: NUBBITU AMRAN GHAYRA SHAKIRIN NIMATI | WA-L-KUFRU MAKHBATHATUN LI-NAFSI AL-MUNIMI. The ajuz is an independent nominal maxim on a resumptive waw. Rejected on the same grounds as 572. I also checked and dismissed weaker candidates: the waw-contrast in bayt 23 (TUMSI WA-TUSBIHU... WA-ABITU...) is waw al-hal, not a new sentence; the FA-clauses in bayts 19, 20, 21, 31, 39, 43 are continuative fa, never terminal; the speech-introducing sites in bayt 65 (after LAHA, i=663) and bayt 66 (after QALAT, i=670) and the embedded cry in bayt 81 (before WAYKA, i=837) are colon-type quotative junctures, not stops; and the parenthesis in bayt 10 (FA-LA TAZUNNI GHAYRAHU) is an interpolated jumla itiradiyya inside a sentence that resumes at BI-MANZILATI. Nothing survives. I therefore return the 89 verse-final boundaries only. All are marked hi: each is the token immediately preceding an NL, or the final token, and the format guarantees these. My whole substantive claim is the negative one -- that no boundary exists between them.
